items.statement: Opt-out automatic referral triggers increase days alive and out of hospital in the 90 days after trigger eligibility by at least 5 days compared with usual referral.
items.rationale: Need is high given the late referrals; novelty is moderate because no lead tests outpatient opt-out triggers; feasibility depends on trigger volume and capacity.
items.risks: Clinic capacity may blunt the effect; eight clinics limit power for small differences.

items.statement: Triggers increase the proportion of eligible patients with a first specialist palliative care visit within 12 weeks.
items.rationale: The direct process effect of the triggers.
items.risks: A process gain can occur without patient benefit.

items.statement: Triggers lengthen the wait for a new palliative care clinic appointment beyond 3 weeks.
items.rationale: The main harm oncologists and the palliative care team fear.
items.risks: Waiting times also move with staffing changes.

summary: Three hypotheses; h1 as the primary question, h2 as the process question and h3 as the balancing question.
